gate.interpretation: Prospective reference reproduction check, not a certified optimum or a stochastic production loss gate. The published POT loss and reproduced author log both use the prescribed-marginal expression; they are compared with an explicit 0.005 tolerance. Actual-marginal raw and repaired full losses are reported separately; the repaired loss must independently be at most 0.025.

caveats: Four-candidate development selection at seed810; confirmation seeds811,812,813 only.
Final saved-rounded criterion retained; no best-checkpoint or retrospective repair-based reselection.
Seed811 continued its original stage; seeds812/813 ran as two additional one-thread workers. Scientific controls and selected prefactors stayed fixed.
Iteration counts are the assessment axis. No method or precision timing comparison is performed.
Both reference and FraMES use float64 throughout; NumPy/POT versus PyTorch implementations and algorithms differ.
Actual saved float64-rounded plan must satisfy combined marginal L1 <=100*eps64; independent repeat repair is reported separately.
Auxiliary NumPy repair uses the frozen reference helper tolerance 1e-12, with its measured residual and 100*eps64 pass/fail retained; it does not control selection or replace saved endpoints.
Solver+current repair excludes instrumentation and previous repairs. Total/process elapsed times are separate.
No original-run timestamp is assigned to the additional post-run float64 repair.
One dataset and three confirmation seeds; ranges are descriptive, not confidence intervals or theorem tests.

precision_comparison.selection_policy: Each precision independently selects the best final saved-rounded objective from the same four candidates at development seed810; no confirmation-based choice.
precision_comparison.caveat: Matching seed numbers are descriptive bookkeeping, not identical sampled-pair paths. The sampling law depends on each evolving coupling, so precision and independently selected prefactors can change later samples. No precision-isolated causal or paired-path equivalence claim.
